plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the architecture of an autoregressive transformer decoder, drawn as a horizontal left-to-right pipeline over a sequence of token positions. At the left, a vertical stack of word-embedding vectors represents the input sequence tokens: <start>, It, takes, great, courage, to, and let. These embeddings enter a large block labeled “Transformer with masked attention,” annotated (× K) to indicate K repeated decoder layers. Inside the transformer block, a lower-triangular masked-attention diagram shows that each token position can attend only to itself and earlier positions, preventing access to future tokens during next-token prediction. The block also shows residual/addition nodes and intermediate feature vectors that pass through the repeated masked-attention layers. At the right, each processed token representation feeds into a “Linear + softmax” block, producing a probability distribution over the vocabulary for the corresponding target token. The target-token labels shown on the far right are It, takes, great, courage, to, let, and yourself, illustrating shifted autoregressive training where the model predicts the next token at each position. This figure introduces the decoder-only transformer architecture for sequence generation, emphasizing causal masking and parallel next-token prediction across positions.

interactionPlan.concept: A decoder-only transformer predicts the next token at every position in parallel, using causally masked self-attention so each position sees only itself and earlier tokens.

Column heading: 'Transformer with masked attention' over a grey rounded rectangle with dashed border
Column heading: 'Linear + softmax'
Column heading: 'Probability of target token'
Left input token labels, top to bottom: <start>, It, takes, great, courage, to, let
Seven horizontal arrows from the input token labels into the embedding container
Seven word-embedding row vectors, each drawn as a row of ~6 empty white cells with black outlines, stacked vertically inside the dashed container
Bracket/bus on the right of the embedding stack collecting all seven rows into one thick arrow entering the transformer block
Masked self-attention panel: tall orange/salmon rounded rectangle containing a lower-triangular fan of straight connection lines from each source row to itself and all rows below it (causal pattern)
Residual skip connection: black line routed over the top of the attention panel into a circled plus (⊕) node
First circled plus (⊕) residual addition node after attention
First teal vertical bar representing the post-attention layer-norm / feature vectors
Position-wise feedforward group: seven small blue-grey rounded pill blocks stacked vertically, each fed by its own short arrow, wrapped by an outer routing rectangle
Second residual skip connection routed over the feedforward group into a second circled plus (⊕)
Second circled plus (⊕) residual addition node after the feedforward
Second teal vertical bar representing the post-feedforward layer-norm output
Annotation '(×K)' with a horizontal ellipsis '···' indicating the decoder block is repeated K times
Seven teal rounded 'Linear + softmax' blocks, one per position, each fed by an arrow from the transformer output bus
Seven output probability rows: blue-grey cells (three cells, dotted ellipsis, two more cells) representing a distribution over the whole vocabulary
Vertical vocabulary axis labels under the first output row: a, aardvark, abacus, ···, zeta, zero
Right-hand target-token labels, top to bottom: It, takes, great, courage, to, let, yourself
Arrows connecting each Linear+softmax block to its probability row
Tooltip/callout panel (appears on click) describing the role of the selected block

interactions.teaches: That the '(×K)' notation is shorthand for K identical stacked decoder blocks, each repeating masked attention + residual add + feedforward, and that depth is a design choice rather than part of the mechanism.
interactions.label: Decoder layers K

interactions.teaches: Why the attention pattern must be lower-triangular: with full bidirectional attention each position could read its own target token, so next-token prediction becomes trivial and the model learns nothing.
interactions.label: Attention pattern

interactions.teaches: The distinct job of each stage — embedding lookup, masked mixing across positions, residual addition, and vocabulary projection — instead of treating the pipeline as one opaque box.

That the row for target 'yourself' is computed from the prefix '<start> … let' only, and that every other row is computed the same way simultaneously — one forward pass yields all next-token predictions.
interactions.label: Trace prediction of 'yourself'

demo_steps.title: The pipeline at a glance
demo_steps.narration: Seven tokens enter as embedding vectors on the left and leave as seven probability distributions over the whole vocabulary on the right. Notice the output labels are the input sequence shifted by one: each position predicts the next token.

demo_steps.title: Inside one decoder block
demo_steps.narration: Click the orange attention panel, the ⊕ nodes, and the teal bars: masked attention mixes information across positions, then each residual addition carries the original vector forward so the block only has to learn a correction.

demo_steps.title: Why the triangle?
demo_steps.narration: Switch to unmasked attention and the connection fan fills in above the diagonal — now the vector at 'let' can see 'yourself', and predicting it is cheating. Switching back restores the lower-triangular causal mask.

demo_steps.title: Unrolling ×K
demo_steps.narration: Increase K and the single block expands into a stack of identical blocks. The shape of the computation never changes; only the number of times the sequence is re-mixed and refined.

demo_steps.title: Tracing one prediction
demo_steps.narration: Step the trace: the prefix '<start> It takes great courage to let' lights up, attention lines flow only from those positions into the last row, residuals add, and the final Linear + softmax produces the distribution whose target is 'yourself'.

demo_steps.title: All predictions at once
demo_steps.narration: Finish the trace and every row highlights: the same forward pass simultaneously predicts It, takes, great, courage, to, let and yourself — this parallel, shifted training is what makes decoder transformers efficient.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The lower-triangular attention pattern is the whole trick: it lets one parallel forward pass produce a next-token prediction at every position without any position ever peeking at its own answer.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Horizontal left-to-right pipeline on white background, four column headings in a serif/LaTeX-like font. Left: seven input token labels with arrows into a dashed-border container holding seven rows of ~6 empty outlined cells; a bracket funnels them into one thick arrow. Center: large light-grey rounded rectangle with dashed border, labelled 'Transformer with masked attention', containing (in order) a tall salmon/orange rounded panel filled with a lower-triangular fan of thin dark lines, a ⊕ node fed by a skip line routed over the panel, a slim teal vertical bar, a group of seven small blue-grey pill blocks each with its own feeder arrow and an outer routing rectangle, a second ⊕ with its own skip line, and a second teal bar. To its right, '(×K)' above a horizontal '···' and an arrow. Right: seven teal rounded 'Linear + softmax' blocks, each arrowing into a probability row of blue-grey cells (three cells, dotted gap, two cells); rotated vocabulary labels a / aardvark / abacus / ··· / zeta / zero beneath the first row; target labels It…yourself at the far right, visibly the input sequence shifted up by one. Highlighting should use a bright accent outline plus dimming of unselected blocks; the trace should pulse along arrows in orange. When K>1, draw repeated compact copies of the decoder block stacked horizontally (or vertically nested) with the '(×K)' badge replaced by layer indices 1…K.

discrepancies: Text is rendered far too small for the inline size: the 1640×600 viewBox is scaled to ~540 px, so column headings (~7 px), token labels (~5.6 px) and vocabulary labels (~4.6 px) are effectively unreadable in the default view, whereas in the source all of these read clearly.

The vocabulary axis labels (a / aardvark / abacus / zeta / zero) are crowded and their rotated baselines sit closer to the cells than in the source, where they hang cleanly below the bottom probability row with even spacing; the '…' dots between them are also placed lower than the label band.

Ghosted 'stacked block' cards appear behind the grey transformer box when K > 1 — an addition not present in the source (acceptable as an interaction affordance, but it changes the composition away from the single dashed box once the demo steps advance K to 4).

Minor proportion drift: the grey masked-attention box and orange attention panel are slightly taller relative to the embedding column than in the source, and the input-token arrows are shorter, leaving less left margin than the original.
evaluation.notes: A structurally excellent, near drop-in reproduction of the decoder-transformer pipeline with correct lower-triangular attention fan, residuals, ×K badge and shifted target labels, plus a rich and pedagogically apt set of interactions (step player, K slider, mask toggle, staged trace); the main weakness is label legibility — at the inline render scale the token, vocabulary and heading text is far too small to read.
action_items: Increase font sizes (headings ~30, token/target labels ~24, vocabulary ~18) or shrink the viewBox width so that all text is comfortably readable when the figure is scaled into a ~600 px container.

Tidy the vocabulary label band: increase vertical offset from the bottom probability row, align all five rotated labels on a common baseline, and move the inter-label ellipsis dots up to sit within that band.
Make the ghost-stack cards subtler (lower opacity / smaller offset) so that advancing K does not visually compete with the single dashed transformer box of the source.
Add a small 'reset view / step 1' affordance or ensure the default (step 0) state always shows K=1 with the causal mask, matching the static source exactly.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (all 5s, no failure modes); remaining issues are implementation details — font sizes, vocabulary label band alignment, and ghost-card styling — which are generator-level fixes.

interactions.teaches: That the '(×K)' notation is shorthand for K identical stacked decoder blocks, each repeating masked attention + residual add + feedforward, and that depth is a design choice rather than part of the mechanism.
interactions.label: Decoder layers K

interactions.teaches: Why the attention pattern must be lower-triangular: with full bidirectional attention each position could read its own target token, so next-token prediction becomes trivial and the model learns nothing.
interactions.label: Attention pattern

interactions.teaches: The distinct job of each stage — embedding lookup, masked mixing across positions, residual addition, and vocabulary projection — instead of treating the pipeline as one opaque box.

That the row for target 'yourself' is computed from the prefix '<start> … let' only, and that every other row is computed the same way simultaneously — one forward pass yields all next-token predictions.
interactions.label: Trace prediction of 'yourself'

demo_steps.title: The pipeline at a glance
demo_steps.narration: Seven tokens enter as embedding vectors on the left and leave as seven probability distributions over the whole vocabulary on the right. Notice the output labels are the input sequence shifted by one: each position predicts the next token.

demo_steps.title: Inside one decoder block
demo_steps.narration: Click the orange attention panel, the ⊕ nodes, and the teal bars: masked attention mixes information across positions, then each residual addition carries the original vector forward so the block only has to learn a correction.

demo_steps.title: Why the triangle?
demo_steps.narration: Switch to unmasked attention and the connection fan fills in above the diagonal — now the vector at 'let' can see 'yourself', and predicting it is cheating. Switching back restores the lower-triangular causal mask.

demo_steps.title: Unrolling ×K
demo_steps.narration: Increase K and the single block expands into a stack of identical blocks. The shape of the computation never changes; only the number of times the sequence is re-mixed and refined.

demo_steps.title: Tracing one prediction
demo_steps.narration: Step the trace: the prefix '<start> It takes great courage to let' lights up, attention lines flow only from those positions into the last row, residuals add, and the final Linear + softmax produces the distribution whose target is 'yourself'.

demo_steps.title: All predictions at once
demo_steps.narration: Finish the trace and every row highlights: the same forward pass simultaneously predicts It, takes, great, courage, to, let and yourself — this parallel, shifted training is what makes decoder transformers efficient.

plan.keyInsight: The lower-triangular attention pattern is the whole trick: it lets one parallel forward pass produce a next-token prediction at every position without any position ever peeking at its own answer.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Horizontal left-to-right pipeline on white background, four column headings in a serif/LaTeX-like font. Left: seven input token labels with arrows into a dashed-border container holding seven rows of ~6 empty outlined cells; a bracket funnels them into one thick arrow. Center: large light-grey rounded rectangle with dashed border, labelled 'Transformer with masked attention', containing (in order) a tall salmon/orange rounded panel filled with a lower-triangular fan of thin dark lines, a ⊕ node fed by a skip line routed over the panel, a slim teal vertical bar, a group of seven small blue-grey pill blocks each with its own feeder arrow and an outer routing rectangle, a second ⊕ with its own skip line, and a second teal bar. To its right, '(×K)' above a horizontal '···' and an arrow. Right: seven teal rounded 'Linear + softmax' blocks, each arrowing into a probability row of blue-grey cells (three cells, dotted gap, two cells); rotated vocabulary labels a / aardvark / abacus / ··· / zeta / zero beneath the first row; target labels It…yourself at the far right, visibly the input sequence shifted up by one. Highlighting should use a bright accent outline plus dimming of unselected blocks; the trace should pulse along arrows in orange. When K>1, draw repeated compact copies of the decoder block stacked horizontally (or vertically nested) with the '(×K)' badge replaced by layer indices 1…K.

In the source the fan of attention lines fully fills the orange panel edge-to-edge with a dense lower-triangular bundle including the long diagonal sweep; the generated fan is sparser/thinner and the panel reads as mostly flat orange at small scale.
Embedding cell rows slightly overflow the dashed container on the right and the connector line exits through the dashed border, whereas the source keeps rows inside with the bus drawn outside.
Plus nodes are drawn as a plain circle with a cross rather than the heavier ⊕ glyph of the source, and are noticeably smaller relative to the teal bars.
evaluation.notes: Structurally a faithful reproduction of the decoder-transformer pipeline with a rich, correct set of interactions (K slider, mask toggle, trace stages, step player), but the drawing renders too small in the stage and the rotated vocabulary labels overlap, hurting legibility.
action_items: Tighten the viewBox / increase the figure's rendered scale (or reduce the reserved vertical whitespace) so token names and column headings read comfortably at inline size.
Re-space the rotated vocabulary labels (a, aardvark, abacus … zeta, zero) so each aligns under its own cell column without overlapping neighbours or the probability row.
Thicken/densify the attention fan and extend it edge-to-edge inside the orange panel to match the source's dense triangular bundle.
Remove or de-emphasise the added 'K = n' sub-caption and ghost layer cards, or gate them behind a step so the default state is a drop-in replacement for the static source.
